sentences.text:
An appeal preferred by the State of Jammu and Kashmir arising out of a decision enhancing compensation in respect of acquisition of lands for a public purpose to the extent of nearly 14 lakhs rupees by making an upward revision of the order of 800%
(from Rs. 1,000 per kanal to Rs. 8,000 per 3 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:021053 2024:PHHC:021053 CRM-M-7752-2024 kanal) which also raised important questions as regards principles of valuation was dismissed as time barred being 4 days beyond time by rejecting an application for condonation of delay.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Hence this appeal by special leave.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: 3. The legislature has conferred the power to condone delay by enacting Section 5 "Any appeal or any application, other than an application under any of the provisions of 0. XXI of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908, may be admitted after the prescribed period if the appellant or the applicant satisfies the Court that he had sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal or making the application within such period." of the Indian Limitation Act of 1963 in order to enable the Courts to do substantial justice to parties by disposing of matters on 'merits'.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text:
The expression "sufficient cause"
employed by the legislature is adequately elastic to enable the Courts to apply the law in a meaningful manner which subserves the ends of justice that being the life-purpose for the existence of the institution of Courts.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is common knowledge that this Court has been making a justifiably liberal approach in matters, instituted in this Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: But the message does not appear to have percolated down to all the other Courts in the hierarchy.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text:
And such a liberal approach is adopted on principle as it is realised that :-
1. Ordinarily a litigant does not stand to benefit by lodging an appeal late.
2. Refusing to condone delay can result in a meritorious matter being thrown out at the very threshold and cause of justice being defeated.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: As against this when delay is condoned the highest that can happen is that a cause would be decided on merits after hearing the parties.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: 3. "Every day's delay must be explained" does not mean that a pedantic approach should be made.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Why not every hour's delay every second's delay ?
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: The 4 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:021053 2024:PHHC:021053 CRM-M-7752-2024 doctrine must be applied in a rational common sense pragmatic manner.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: 4. When substantial justice and technical considerations are pitted against each other, cause of substantial justice deserves to be preferred for the other side cannot claim to have vested right in injustice being done because of a non-deliberate delay.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: 5. There is no presumption that delay is occasioned deliberately, or on account of culpable negligence, or on account of mala fides.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: A litigant does not stand to benefit by resorting to delay.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: In fact he runs a serious risk.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: 6. It must be grasped that judiciary is respected not on account of its power to legalise injustice on technical grounds but because it is capable of removing injustice and is expected to do so.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Making a justice-oriented approach from this perspective, there was sufficient cause for condoning the delay in the institution of the appeal.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: The fact that it was the 'State', which was seeking condonation and not a private party was altogether irrelevant.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: The doctrine of equality before law demands that all litigants, including the State as a litigant, are accorded the same treatment and the law is administered in an even-handed manner.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: There is no warrant for according a stepmotherly treatment when the 'State' is the applicant praying for condonation of delay.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: In fact experience shows that on account of an impersonal machinery (no one in charge of the matter is directly hit or hurt by the judgment sought to be subjected to appeal) and the inherited bureaucratic methodology imbued with the note-making, file pushing, and passing on the buck ethos, delay on its part is less difficult to understand though more difficult to approve.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: In any event, the State which represents 5 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:021053 2024:PHHC:021053 CRM-M-7752-2024 the collective cause of the community, does not deserve a litigant non grata status.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: The Courts therefore have to informed with the spirit and philosophy of the provision in the course of the interpretation of the expression "sufficient cause".
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: So also the same approach has to be evidenced in its application to matters at hand with the end in view to do even-handed justice on merits in preference to the approach which scuttles a decision on merits.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Turning to the facts of the matter giving rise to the present appeal, we are satisfied that sufficient cause exists for the delay.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: The order of the High Court dismissing the appeal before it as time barred, is therefore, set aside.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Delay is condoned.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: And the matter is remitted to the High Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: The High Court will now dispose of the appeal on merits after affording reasonable opportunity of hearing to both the sides.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: 4. Appeal is allowed accordingly.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: No costs.
sentences._hearing_file: Sandeep vs State Of Haryana on 14 February, 2024.json

sentences.text: Appeal allowed."

Coming back to the facts of the instant case, it is apparent from the record that after charges came to be framed against the petitioner and his two co-accused namely Ishwar and Rounoq filed a revision petition with a delay of 26 days before the Court of ASJ, Panipat which came to be allowed and the petitioner therein stood discharged.

So far as the petitioner is concerned,
he filed a revision petition with a delay of 131 days.

employed by the legislature is adequately elastic to enable the Courts to apply the law in a meaningful manner which subserves the ends of justice that being the life-purpose for the existence of the institution of Courts.
As against this when delay is condoned the highest that can happen is that a cause would be decided on merits after hearing the parties.
4. When substantial justice and technical considerations are pitted against each other, cause of substantial justice deserves to be preferred for the other side cannot claim to have vested right in injustice being done because of a non-deliberate delay.
5. There is no presumption that delay is occasioned deliberately, or on account of culpable negligence, or on account of mala fides.
A litigant does not stand to benefit by resorting to delay.
In fact he runs a serious risk.
6. It must be grasped that judiciary is respected not on account of its power to legalise injustice on technical grounds but because it is capable of removing injustice and is expected to do so.
Making a justice-oriented approach from this perspective, there was sufficient cause for condoning the delay in the institution of the appeal.
The fact that it was the 'State', which was seeking condonation and not a private party was altogether irrelevant.
The doctrine of equality before law demands that all litigants, including the State as a litigant, are accorded the same treatment and the law is administered in an even-handed manner.
There is no warrant for according a stepmotherly treatment when the 'State' is the applicant praying for condonation of delay.
The cause of substantial justice deserves to be preferred over technical considerations.
